learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">A human male is heterozygous for autosomal gene A
B and G he is also hemizygous for haemophilic gene h. What proportion of his sperm will be abgH<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"The correct answer is: 4. 0.
Explanation:
  • The human male is heterozygous for autosomal genes A, B, and G. This means his genotype for these genes is Abg (he has one dominant and one recessive allele for each gene).
  • The male is also hemizygous for the hemophilic gene h (which is an X-linked gene). Hemizygous means that for X-linked genes, males only have one copy of the gene (since they have one X chromosome and one Y chromosome).
Now, the male's genotype is:
  • Abg for the autosomal genes (A, B, and G).
  • h for the X-linked hemophilic gene (since he is hemizygous for it, he carries one h allele on his X chromosome).
For sperm production:
  • Males will pass either an X or a Y chromosome to their offspring.
  • If the sperm carries an X chromosome, it will carry the h allele, and if it carries a Y chromosome, it will carry no h allele (since the Y chromosome doesn't carry the hemophilic gene).
For the sperm to have the genotype abgH, the H allele would have to come from the X chromosome, but since the male is hemizygous with the h allele, he can only pass on the h allele, not the H allele.
Thus, no sperm will carry the abgH genotype, because the male only has the h allele to pass on, not the H allele.
So, the correct proportion of sperm with the abgH genotype is 0."

The correct answer is 2: A, B, AB and O

Explanation:

  • A man with blood group "A" can have genotypes IAIA or IAIO.
  • A woman with blood group "B" can have genotypes IBIB or IBIO.

To find all possible blood groups, we need to consider all possible combinations:

  • IAIA x IBIB → IAIB (AB)
  • IAIA x IBIO → IAIB (AB), IAIO (A)
  • IAIO x IBIB → IAIB (AB), IBIO (B)
  • IAIO x IBIO → IAIB (AB), IAIO (A), IBIO (B), IOIO (O)

Therefore, the possible blood groups of their offspring are A, B, AB, and O.
